note: Tuesday 3 Nov 2026 07:02 SGT run. Fear & Greed ticked down to 25/Fear (components still dominated by near-zero Safe-Haven Demand and deep Market Momentum/Volatility fear) even as Monday's S&P decline was mild (-0.51%) -- the VIX's +8.91% jump signals options markets pricing more fear than the cash tape shows. Breadth is a genuine broad-vs-narrow split: full-NYSE tape stayed decliner-led with new lows still outpacing new highs, while the narrower S&P1500+Nasdaq100 constituent set and small/mid-caps rallied on the oil-crash-driven cyclical rotation into energy-cost-sensitive sectors. Flows are unchanged from the week-ending-Oct-28 EPFR/Lipper cut -- the next release (due ~Nov 5-6) is the first to capture Friday's selloff, Monday's VIX spike and the crude crash.

flows.narrative: Reconfirmed this run: no newer weekly fund-flow cut has published since week-ending-Oct-28. That week showed global equity funds +$56.2B (BofA Flow Show) entirely via passive ETF buying (+$75.9B) against an active-fund outflow (-$19.6B), China the standout at +$25.7B (largest since Apr 2025), Europe at -$2.3B (worst since July), and gold funds' first outflow since July (-$1.7B). None of this reflects the past week's AI-capex shock, VIX spike, crude crash, or midterm-election week; the next release (Thu/Fri Nov 5-6) is the one to watch.
